messages:
elaine: Quick heads-up — did a fast bring-up for aurora-14b (hosted + local quant builds). Wanted a short cost-vs-quality scan for GTN recommendations and product routing. @samir @ryan @maria

samir: Nice. which eval slices did you run? short answers or long-form?

ryan: Ran three slices: short_qa (500 q), summarization (200 docs, mixed lengths), conv_recall (1k turns). Also a small safety/tox check.

eval-bot: SUMMARY: models tested: aurora-14b fp16, aurora-14b int8, aurora-14b int4
- latency (p50/p95, single-token streaming on gpus): fp16 120ms/260ms | int8 85ms/210ms | int4 60ms/190ms
- throughput (tokens/sec): fp16 950 | int8 1600 | int4 2400
- est cost per 1M tokens (unit econ, infra only): fp16 $24.8 | int8 $8.9 | int4 $4.2

- short_qa (accuracy %): fp16 86.2 | int8 81.9 (-4.3) | int4 69.8 (-16.4)
- summarization (ROUGE-L): fp16 46.1 | int8 44.7 (-1.4) | int4 40.0 (-6.1)
- conv_recall (F1): fp16 78.5 | int8 74.3 (-4.2) | int4 62.7 (-15.8)
- safety: no new flags for fp16/int8; int4 had higher hallucination on knowledge checks (~+3%)

maria: TL;DR — int8 buys ~2.8x cost reduction with small quality hit (~4 pts on QA), int4 is cheap but risky for recall and knowledge tasks.

elaine: Exactly. Also measured stability across prompt length: int8 degrades slightly on longer context (>600 tokens), more inconsistent for retrieval-augmented prompts. int4 almost always worse after 400 tokens.

samir: For GTN/product, do we want to recommend int8 as default low-cost route? Or keep fp16 as default and expose int8 as opt-in?

ryan: My vote: recommend int8 as default for latency-sensitive user-facing flows that are tolerant of minor accuracy drops (search, short Q&A quick answers). Keep fp16 for high-precision flows (billing, legal, medical). int4 -> only for bulk offline generation and caching pipelines.

maria: +1. Also propose a canary: run 10% traffic through fp16 for top intents (payment support, account changes) and monitor regression. We can wire auto-fallback to fp16 for low-confidence outputs.

elaine: Proposed routing config for GTN (informal):
- route A (interactive short answers): aurora-int8 primary, aurora-fp16 fallback on low-confidence or high-safety intent
- route B (summaries, legal): aurora-fp16 primary
- route C (bulk batch gen): aurora-int4 with sampling QA + periodic fp16 validation

- Recommendation on pricing guidance for GTN: use infra unit costs + 25% platform/ops margin -> suggest tenant-facing rate approx: fp16 $0.035 / 1k tokens, int8 $0.0125 / 1k, int4 $0.006 (rounded). These align with our committed capacity economics.

samir: Nice. Two follow-ups: can we get a small eval set of product-critical prompts to run against int8 canary? and can eng-runtime add a confidence score hook for easy fallback?

ryan: I'll assemble a 150-query product-critical set (privacy scrubbed) and push to eval infra tomorrow. @eng-runtime: can we add a low-lift hook to return token-level confidence or log probability?

elaine: Filing a small follow-up ticket for GTN docs + pricing draft. If no objections, I'll push these recs to product by EOD and start the canary. :thumbsup:

maria: No objections from me — go for canary. :rocket:

ryan: +1

samir: +1

elaine: Thanks all — will update thread with canary metrics next week.
